newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU stability council must not be exclusive - Juncke.
newsitem.headline: EMU stability council must not be exclusive - Juncke.

text.p: A stability council among countries joining European monetary union must establish links with those not qualifying at the start date, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Monday.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Juncker said: "I think this will have to be an informal structure of those who are in (economic and monetary union)."
"But we do not have the right to put in an exclusive structure."

Juncker said there was broad agreement within the EU's 15-nation bloc over the principle of such a council, a French-led idea to allow for closer consultation on economic policy within a monetary union.
He noted, however, that Germany and France had different visions over how such a council would operate in practice.
"They have different traditions and behaviours," Juncker said. "They have to have a more common vision."
Juncker also criticised recent public statements by EU officials which sought to play down the chances of some countries to meet the Maastricht criteria.
"I think you can't criticise a member state who wants to part of monetary union," Juncker added. "Why should we discourage member states when they are trying to meet the criteria."
